title: List traversal retains the whole list: range/iterate + count/foldl cost ~10µs per cell and grow superlinearly
description:
Measured on master cb1cc36, release build, with and without lib/prelude.blob (cargo xtask prelude-compile): no difference.

- x: range(0, 100000) count — 1.17s; range(0, 400000) count — 4.3s; range(0, 4000000) count — 95s (superlinear: ~24µs/cell).
- eu -S on range(0, 400000) count: 45.2M ticks (~113/cell), 9.6M allocs (~24/cell), 9 collections, Mark 1.38s, Blocks Recycled 0, Peak Blocks 26,937.
- Same shape for iterate(+ 1, 0) take(400000) count (4.27s, Recycled 0) and range(0, 400000) foldl(+, 0) (4.09s, Recycled 0).

Blocks Recycled 0 with peak blocks growing with n suggests the consumed list prefix stays reachable (space leak), so each GC marks an ever larger live set.

Lane diagnosis so far (measured-single): not a regression (5aa27b7, before #1247/#1242, is the same); the list itself is retained; ~113 ticks/cell is the normal shape and the superlinear part is GC mark on a growing live set; triggered by advancing a list while calling a function-valued parameter (count/foldl-strict via op) — a global callee, no call, or a counter runs in constant space. Exact pinning root not yet found.

AoC risk: any puzzle walking a few million list cells takes minutes. Found by the AoC 2026 solutions-repository lane.

(Restored by the coordinator: this bead's content was overwritten on 17 Nov by a lane with a stale store; that lane's decision bead is now eu-oaz72.178.)

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
[re-relayed by coordinator 17 from refused branch beads-inbox/20261117T111452Z-eu-oaz72-175]
Diagnosis (interim, measured-single, release build, master cb1cc36, source prelude).
(b) Not a regression from #1247/#1242: binary built at 5aa27b7 (before both) gives the same peak blocks and ticks for range(0,200000) count and the minimal loops below. (#1251 strict-prelude build not completed.)
(a) The consumed prefix IS retained (Recycled 0, peak grows with n, sweep ~0). Retention is the LIST (a CAF-held list of the same length costs MORE blocks than the loop: 16.4k vs 11.8k at n=200k), not the loop frames. Hand-written loops over the same list run in constant space (peak 1,026) unless the loop calls an unknown function parameter: fs(op,l): if(l nil?,0,seq(op(0),fs(op,l tail))) retains; same with op called directly (global add) or no call at all: constant. A counter loop with the same op call does not retain; a list loop that does not call op does not retain. So the trigger is list advance + call of a function-valued parameter (count/foldl-strict call op(i, l head)).
Stack at GC (temporary instrumentation, reverted) shows two Update continuations and a SeqBind persisting for the whole loop, i.e. an in-flight thunk whose env frame can pin its sibling slots (the list-argument thunk, updated in place to the head cons). Not yet proven that this frame is the pin.
Refuted as sole cause: (1) make_arg_array wrapping evaluated cons/native slots in Atom aliases (200k wraps; making them settled removes the wraps, peak unchanged); (2) Global/Value arg atoms capturing caller env; (3) memoising Atom-alias callee slots in enter_local (fires once). 
(c) ~113 ticks/cell: hand-written len loop over take(up) is ~97 ticks/cell, so the tick count is the expected shape for this prelude code; the leak, not ticks, is the superlinear part (mark time grows with live set).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
[re-relayed by coordinator 17 from refused branch beads-inbox/20261117T111452Z-eu-oaz72-175]
Interim handoff: branch eu-oaz72.175/list-retention (docs only) holds docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-17-list-retention-diagnosis.md and the tracer patch. Tracer on a counter+list loop (d1) shows a frame chain from the running frame via the l parameter = non-update Case closure over the previous frame; but d1 is the lazy-accumulator shape (l demand is Lazy,AtMostOnce), so the tracer must be re-run on range(0,n) count itself. Suspect: update-elided (AtMostOnce) argument closures that are seq-forced and passed on (compiler.rs take_lambda_form / strict_thunk_indices). No fix implemented.

title: A call missing a comma is accepted and renders {} (errors/x018 pins exit 0)
description: Found by sweep 6 (eu-wv5b3, #1298) while pinning error sidecars: tests/harness/errors/x018* exits 0 and its sidecar pins that. Scope not ruled; silent wrong answers, so a candidate for 0.16.0.

title: str.split-on is quadratic: ~27s on ~3.7k elements
description: Found while revising the AoC 2025 solutions (#1283): prelude split-on takes about 27s on a list of ~3.7k elements, i.e. quadratic in the list length (measured-single, noisy machine). Also noted there: split-when splits only once, and over-sliding-pairs via window is ~2x slower than zip-with against tail. Acceptance: split-on is linear (show timings across sizes under the eucalypt-performance protocol), behaviour unchanged, gating harness test for its results. Touches lib/prelude.eu: wait for the prelude slot. In 0.16.0 by decision 68.
notes: Coordinator: split-on is str.split-on (lib/prelude.eu:1101, `split flip`), so the cost may sit in the split intrinsic rather than prelude code. Reproduce on the #1283 input first (examples/aoc25, before 6bff305 replaced it) to confirm which side is quadratic.

title: eu doc follow-ups after #1305: scoping blocks expose helpers; suppressed namespaces; one-level --output-dir pages; prelude.version undocumented
description: From #1305 (eu-oaz72.193), all pre-existing: (a) a top-level scoping block m: {..}.result still exposes its helpers in eu doc output; (b) single-file markdown skips export: :suppress namespaces but the prelude pages publish them; (c) --output-dir prelude pages expand only one namespace level. Also eu.prelude.version (lib/prelude.eu) is now counted undocumented (coverage 431/432) — a one-line doc string fixes it, needs the prelude slot. Scope not ruled.

title: Prelude nub-by is quadratic (seen ++ [k], result ++ [x], any over seen)
description: Found by the eu-oaz72.192 lane (#1296): nub-by (lib/prelude.eu ~1897) uses the same quadratic foldl pattern that made list split-on take 8.4s on 4k elements — appending to seen and result per element and scanning seen with any. Fix like #1296 (reversed accumulators; a set/dict for seen where the key is hashable). Touches lib/prelude.eu: needs the prelude slot. Scope not ruled (sibling of eu-oaz72.192, which decision 68 put in 0.16.0).

title: EDN import: unsuffixed integers above i64::MAX are rejected by the edn-format parser (BadInt)
description: From #1291 (eu-1yv37). eu never emits this form (it uses the N suffix), but third-party EDN may contain e.g. 9999999999999999999 without N; edn-format rejects it with BadInt before eu's importer sees it. Needs a pre-parse step or an upstream change. Also: EDN InvalidNumber errors carry no source span (edn-format values have none). Scope not ruled.

title: Checker: block-param detection ignores type guards (h(x): x block? then(x.a, 0); h(3) warns)
description: From #1290 review (eu-oaz72.172 follow-up). detect_block_params in src/core/typecheck/check.rs treats a parameter projected with .a as a block even when the projection is guarded by block?, so h(x): x block? then(x.a, 0) with h(3) gives a false warning. Pre-existing, but #1286 widened it to block-wrapped bodies. Needs flow-sensitive narrowing (guarded branches don't count as block uses). In 0.16.0 as a checker false warning (decision 65 brings checker false warnings in), and because #1286 widened it.

title: Checker: type list-destructuring parameters as tuples so list-block(5) warns
description: From #1286/#1290 review (eu-oaz72.172). After #1286 a list-destructuring parameter is typed any, so list-block(5) no longer warns (the old warning was accidental). Typing [a, b] parameters as tuples would restore a genuine warning. Separate checker feature; scope not ruled (not labelled 0.16.0).

title: eu doc nested namespaces: leftovers from #1284
description: Left after #1284 (eu-oaz72.185) merged: (1) doc coverage counts two levels while rendering goes deeper; (2) an undocumented sub-namespace drops its members' docs; (3) markdown heading level stops at depth 6 instead of clamping; (4) docs/reference/cli.md lacks a sentence on namespace members. Blocks returned by functions stay excluded by design. In 0.16.0 by decision 68.
